text: haha SHIT it buckled 10 faces but i think i just create face instead maybe
resolution: User reported that solidify buckled ~10 faces on the front opening and suspected they should have used Create face instead. Advised — no code changed. Confirmed: this is exactly the thin/tight self-intersection footgun flagged earlier (solidify insets each face inward 0.125m, so faces collide and invert on a tight spot). For closing an opening the correct tool is Create face, which adds zero thickness and cannot buckle. Recovery: Ctrl+Z once (solidify is a single undoable commit, so one undo removes all buckled faces), then Create face across the front opening and Flip if needed. Gave the durable rule: Create face = close a hole/add a wall (flat, never buckles); solidify = thicken an existing shell (only where there's room, never thin/tight faces). Re-offered to add a thin-part guard to solidify (refuse or auto-thin) now that the user has hit the failure for real.
